input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: `raise cause ... from None` sets __suppress_context__ and clears the re-raised exception's own __cause__
- failure path: the retried function raises ValueError from KeyError, catches it and raises TryAgain; with reraise=True the ValueError that reaches the caller has lost its KeyError cause, so the root cause disappears from the traceback

Reviewer finding
- description: The reraise path raises the cause with `from None`, which sets `__suppress_context__` and clears the cause on the underlying exception. The code also takes `__context__` as a fallback, so it can pick up an unrelated implicit context.
- rationale: Trigger: a user raises TryAgain inside an except block (cause set via `from` or context set implicitly), and retries are exhausted with reraise=True. `raise cause ... from None` mutates the cause exception, setting `__cause__` to None and `__suppress_context__` to True, so any chain the original exception had is hidden in the traceback. Using `__context__` can also surface an unrelated exception that happened to be active when TryAgain was raised, instead of the TryAgain itself.
critique: The finding names the same faulty operation, `raise cause ... from None`. It describes the same failure: the re-raised underlying exception has its `__cause__` cleared and context suppressed, so its original chain (here ValueError from KeyError) disappears from the traceback. The extra point about the `__context__` fallback is additional, but the core mechanism matches.
